author: Souter
last_counted: Aponte Matos v. Toledo Dávila; First Circuit No. 97-1645.; 1998-02-26; Ginsburg
form: One signed plenary lead with association, free-exercise, equality and bounded-mandate parts, with three substantively distinct separate writings
authority: Stevens assigns as the senior Associate in the actual vacatur and bounded-remand coalitions. Stone expressly does not reach the association and free-exercise claims and proposes a distinct formal reversal and intermediate-scrutiny equality instruction, rather than the five-Justice vacatur/ordinary-rationality mandate. His common preference to set aside the equality defense judgment is not converted into a join in that different formal mandate. The Chief's balance policy does not bind this Associate assignment; actual counts, eligibility and the corresponding pool are nevertheless recorded.
fit: Souter writes for the concrete coordination demonstrated in his Umbehr, Jeffries and Romer opinions: actual protected activity, a justified employment restriction, personal causal proof and the independent ordinary-equality inquiry. The separate Brown/Lukumi religion ground must remain distinct rather than merging every right into Pickering. Breyer is the strongest equal-count alternative through his full Jeffries/Brown joins and actual-function analysis; Souter's authored treatment of the specific employment/equality boundaries supplies the closer fit. All five common joiners can carry every part; O'Connor can join the free-exercise part but not the whole lead. Stevens assigns the complete opinion to one full supporter, without artificial splitting. O'Connor's own separate statement preserves her differentiated association/equality position; Scalia states the common assumed-right and secular-ground dissent with Thomas. Stone's equality concurrence preserves his approved proposed standard and express nonreach.
count_effect: The one signed plenary lead counts once for Souter; all three separate writings are excluded.
